Bartolome @Joseph Molina | Approved pending prioritisation |  *(blank)* | @Dani Rivett 's commentary on the ticket: " The content team are really keen to be able to have this feature to execute numerous SEO requests and to build long-term page rankings for popular searches." |

Note (my observation): **none of the three carries a BED/DEV number.** SFCC-173 and SFCC-174 have no BED line at all; SFCC-724's BED and Testing cells hold *names instead of numbers* — i.e. unestimated, assigned to Victor Crisostomo (BED) and Krizel Bartolome / Joseph Molina (Testing).

### 1b. The capacity table — verbatim

Preceding narrative, quoted exactly:
> **Enhancement Capacity**
>
> We have 2 sprints of Enhancements capacity, equivalent to 20 business days. With four disciplines involved — 1 x BA, 1 x FED, 1 x BED, and 1 x Testing — this gives us a combined total of 80 business days.
>
> To date the following amount has been approved by Zimmermann team and consumed:

| *(blank)* | **BA** | **FED** | **DEV** | **QA** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SFCC-155 | 0.5 days | 1 day | 1 day | 2 days |
| SFCC-143 | 0.5 days | 2 days | 2 days | 2 days |
| SFCC-142 | 1 day | 3.5 days | 3.5 days | 2 days |
| SFCC-133 | 0.5 days | 3 days | 3 days | 3 days |
| **SFCC-173** | **0.5 days** | **3 days** | **N/A** | **3 days** |
| **Total Consumed as of** | 3 days | 12.5 days | 9.5 days | 12 days |
| **Total Remaining** | 17 days | 7.5 days | 10.5 days | 8 days |

(The header cell reads literally "**Total Consumed as of**" with nothing after "of" — an unrendered date macro or an unfinished sentence. There is no as-at date on the totals.)

### 1c. VERDICT ON THE CLAIM: **TRUE**

SFCC-173's FED 3 days is a line item in the consumed table and is arithmetically inside the 12.5-day FED total, while the same ticket's Status in the enhancements table above is `TBC`.

Proof by arithmetic on the quoted figures:

| | BA | FED | DEV | QA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sum of the 5 listed rows | 0.5+0.5+1+0.5+0.5 = **3** | 1+2+3.5+3+3 = **12.5** | 1+2+3.5+3+N/A = **9.5** | 2+2+2+3+3 = **12** |
| Page's stated total | 3 | 12.5 | 9.5 | 12 |
| **Match?** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

Every column reconciles exactly *including* the SFCC-173 row. Strip SFCC-173 out and FED consumed becomes **9.5 days**, remaining **10.5 days** — not the 12.5 / 7.5 the page states. So the 3 FED days are unambiguously counted.

**The inconsistency is sharper than the claim suggests.** The consumed table is not driven by the Status column in either direction:

- **One `TBC` row is counted:** SFCC-173.
- **Five `Approved`-family rows are NOT counted:** SFCC-135 (Approved, FED+BED 7 days), SFCC-704 (Approved), SFCC-859 (Approved, FED 5 days), SFCC-946 (Approved), SFCC-935 (Approved - review BED estimate) — plus SFCC-724 (Approved pending prioritisation, FED 5 days).
- **SFCC-174 is also `TBC` with identical sizing to SFCC-173** (BA 0.5 / FED 3 / Testing 3) and is **not** in the consumed table.

So two rows with the same status and the same numbers are treated oppositely. That asymmetry is the finding, not just the TBC inclusion.

**Second, separate discrepancy I found — SFCC-142.** Its enhancements-table sizing reads `BA: 1 day  FED + BED: 5 days  QA: 3 days`, but the consumed table records FED 3.5 + DEV 3.5 = **7 days** (not 5) and QA **2 days** (not 3). The other four rows reconcile cleanly against their sizing cells. On the quoted figures, FED consumed is overstated by ~1.5 days on this row independently of the SFCC-173 question.

### 1d. Status legend: **NONE EXISTS**

There is no legend, key, or definition of the Status values anywhere on the page. `TBC`, `Approved`, `Approved pending prioritisation`, `Pending prioritisation`, `Agreed/ Understood`, `Understood`, `Deferred to Phase 2`, `Descoped`, `Approved - review BED estimate`, `N/A` and blank all appear with no explanation of what any of them mean or which qualify for the capacity totals.

The only text bearing on inclusion is the one sentence quoted above — *"To date the following amount has been approved by Zimmermann team and consumed"* — which asserts the listed items are approved. **SFCC-173 contradicts that framing on the same page.**

### 1e. Last-updated date and author: **NOT RETRIEVABLE**

The MCP server returns empty strings for `created` and `updated` and exposes no author/`by` field, across three different retrieval paths (`confluence_get_page` with metadata, `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_page_history` v17). Only `version: 17` is available. Not a connection failure — the fields come back present-but-empty. You'd need the Confluence UI or REST API directly.

---

## TASK 2 — Confluence SEO strategy pages

### Pages found

| Page | ID | Bears on |
|---|---|---|
| **04.1.19 Data Migration / SEO / Analytics Requirements - Mapping** | 478248974 | The live DMU→story traceability matrix (DMU-022…043 → SFCC-562…577) + a "what's needed to progress" column. Richest source. |
| **04.1.14 Data Migration, SEO, GEO and URL** | 302710811 | Signed-off source requirements with Zimmermann's own business comments. |
| **Technical Solution Design – PWA** | 256835585 | §8.1–8.6 SSR/SEO/GEO architecture; §8.4 enumerates the JSON-LD types. |
| **04.4.3 Product Category Taxonomy** | 380043284 | L1–L4 category URL tree with per-category "No Index" flags. Status: In progress. |
| **6. Site URLs & SEO Configuration** | 339837017 | BM pre-launch config checklist. No per-filter rules. |
| **04.1.9 Search and Recommendations** | 303661057 | Facet behaviour (SPR-19…32/68). No SEO rules. |
| **9.2 Enhancements** | 385318913 | (Task 1.) Only mention of AI extraction in the space. |

### (b) What tool performs "AI answer extraction" — **NOT NAMED ANYWHERE. Still open.**

This was flagged as the important one, so to be explicit: **Confluence does not answer it.** Exactly one page in space SFCC mentions AI extraction, and it records it as the *same open question* SFCC-174 is asking — page 385318913, SFCC-174's Notes cell, quoted:

> **"Outstanding - what tool is doing this AI extraction?**  @Emma Kirwan to check with Miranda  Needs to be for PLP (exists today), but if beyond PLP or something else, then we need to confirm"

A CQL text search for `"AI extraction"` across the space returns only that page plus one unrelated Discovery deck attachment. Searches for *answer engine*, *AI bots*, *GEO / generative engine optimisation*, and *Miranda* surfaced no vendor. No page in the space identifies who Miranda is or what organisation she belongs to.

Three named external parties exist — **Sparro** (SEO consultancy), **Tell No Lies** (martech/GTM partner), and an unnamed TBC accessibility vendor. **None is described as performing AI answer extraction.**

Adjacent evidence from Jira that reframes the question (**my inference, flagged as such**): **SFCC-175 "SEO – AI Search Monitoring and Share-of-Voice Tracking Integration"** describes *"Data integration hooks to support AI search monitoring and share-of-voice tracking across ChatGPT Shopping, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews"* — and its own description field records **Status: Out of Scope**, labels `ENH-051`, `FutureRoadmap`. So the *consuming surfaces* are named (ChatGPT Shopping, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) but the *monitoring tool* that would verify extraction is the story that's been put out of scope. My read: the SFCC-174 question may be conflating "which AI surface consumes the structured fields" (answered: those three) with "what tool do we test/monitor extraction with" (unanswered, and its enabling story is out of scope). That's an inference, not a document statement.

Also relevant: **TSD §8.6**, quoted — *"No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation."* GEO is deliberately foundations-only.

### (a) FAQ / Article structured data — **NOT SPECIFIED, NOT IN THE REQUIREMENTS BASELINE**

No `FAQPage`, `Article`, `HowTo` or `QAPage` schema appears anywhere in the space. I independently confirmed this against the full DMU list on page 478248974: the schema requirements are DMU-038 (Product/Merchant Listing, PDP), DMU-039 (CollectionPage/BreadcrumbList/ItemList, PLP), DMU-040 (LocalBusiness, boutiques), DMU-041 (Organisation, homepages), DMU-042 (sizes/availability). **There is no FAQ or Article requirement.**

The complete specified set, from TSD §8.4 (ID 256835585), quoted:
> "Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:
> * **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
> * **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
> * **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
> * **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`)."

Template ownership splits: **PDP schema template from Tell No Lies; PLP, boutique and homepage templates from Sparro.** Nothing is buildable yet — DMU-038's progress note reads *"Schema template to be provided by Tell No Lies. No JSON-LD exists anywhere yet — clean build once it lands."*

**Consequence for SFCC-173 (my inference):** FAQ/Article schema has no DMU requirement behind it and no agency template in flight. It exists only as enhancement `ENH-049`. It is genuinely net-new scope, not a variation on SFCC-572/573.

**Doc conflict worth flagging:** the TSD's third-party table credits Sparro with *"the JSON-LD schema templates (PDP, PLP, boutique, homepage — DMU-037 to DMU-040)"*, which contradicts 04.1.19/04.1.14 (PDP → Tell No Lies) and is off-by-one on DMU numbering throughout. Treat 04.1.14/04.1.19 as authoritative. TSD §8.4 also adds `WebSite` and `ClothingStore` types no DMU requirement mentions.

### (c) Indexable filter page URL rules / per-filter metadata — **DEFAULT RULE SPECIFIED, EXCEPTION AND METADATA ABSENT**

**Specified:**
- DMU-023, quoted: *"The system will apply canonical tags on all filtered and faceted PLP URLs pointing back to the unfiltered base PLP URL to prevent duplicate content indexation."*
- DMU-037: robots.txt *"restricts crawling of… filtered URL parameters."*
- TSD §8.1.1: *"Search results, filtered PLP states | SSR shell + CSR data | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven"*
- TSD §8.5 page URL formats: *"Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix)"*.

**Unresolved — the live gap.** Page 478248974, DMU-023 "What's needed to progress", quoted:
> "Blanket canonical-to-base risks suppressing facet pages with real search demand (e.g. \"blue dresses\"). Merged into SFCC-562 (was SFCC-563) — need Tell No Lies/Sparro to confirm which facet combos should stay indexable, everything else defaults to canonical."

Page 302710811, DMU-023 Comments column — Zimmermann's own words:
> "We would like to control updating the canonical as needed on indexible filter pages"

**Absent entirely from Confluence:**
- **Any URL structure for an indexable filter page.** Nothing states whether these are query params (`?colour=blue`), path segments (`/dresses/blue`), or SFCC category URLs.
- **Any per-filter title, meta description, H1 or copy rule.** The closest is category-level: DMU-036 (*"CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level"*), SPR-03 and SPR-04.

---

## TASK 3 — Jira issue details

**Field note:** ACs are in `customfield_10231`, confirmed working — it returned real content for SFCC-562, 571, 568, 569, 573. Where I report a null below, that is a genuine empty field, not a retrieval failure.

### SFCC-563 — "SEO — Canonical Tags on Filtered & Faceted PLP URLs"
Status `To Do` · Labels `Custom`, `DMU-023`, `Squad-B`

**This story is dead.** Description, quoted:
> "MERGED INTO SFCC-562 as of 2026-09-14 - do not groom this story separately. All requirement detail, acceptance criteria, and technical notes now live on SFCC-562.
>
> Original description, retained for reference:
>
> As a Site Admin, I want canonical tags on all filtered and faceted PLP URLs pointing back to the unfiltered base PLP URL, so that duplicate content from filter/facet parameter combinations does not dilute the authority of the canonical PLP.
>
> Per FR comment: Zimmermann want the ability to control and update the canonical on indexable filter pages via BM where needed. This BM configurability should be scoped into this story. Depends on SFCC-562 (canonical tags on all indexable pages)."

**Acceptance criteria: `null`. AC count: 0.**

> **This matters for your audit framing.** Any claim of the form "SFCC-724 is covered by SFCC-563 + SFCC-577" cannot be evaluated as stated — SFCC-563 has been an empty shell since 2026-09-14. The real comparison is **SFCC-562 + SFCC-577**.

### SFCC-562 — "SEO — Canonical Tags on All Indexable Pages"
Status `To Do` · Labels `Custom`, `DMU-022`, `DMU-023`, `SPR-03`, `Squad-B`

Description, quoted:
> "As a Site Admin, I want canonical tags output on all indexable pages, referencing the preferred URL for that storefront, so that duplicate content is avoided and link equity is correctly attributed to the canonical URL.
>
> Covers both DMU-022 (canonical on all indexable pages) and DMU-023 (canonical on filtered/faceted PLP URLs pointing to the base PLP) - merged into one story since they're a single implementation surface with a shared codepath (one function, one extra branch for the filtered case). Zimmermann also want the ability to override the canonical target on specific indexable filter pages via Business Manager - scoped into this story.
>
> Merged from SFCC-563 on 2026-09-14 (see Confluence page 478248974 footer comment for the rationale). SFCC-563 is retained in Jira as a superseded reference only - do not groom it separately."

**Acceptance criteria — 9 discrete ACs**, quoted in full:
> - Every indexable page (homepage, PDP, unfiltered PLP/category, content pages) renders exactly one self-referencing canonical link tag in the page head, using the absolute https URL for the current storefront/locale.
> - No page renders more than one canonical tag.
> - Paginated PLP/category pages (page 2, 3, etc.) each carry their OWN self-referencing canonical - never canonicalized back to page 1 (per Google: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading).
> - Filtered/faceted PLP URLs (colour/size/category filter combinations with no confirmed standalone search value) render a canonical tag pointing to the unfiltered base PLP URL, not a self-reference.
> - Facet combinations Tell No Lies/Sparro confirm as having real standalone search demand (see SFCC-571 dependency) are excluded from that rule and get a self-referencing canonical instead, per SFCC-571's per-facet-type split - never both a robots.txt block and a canonical on the same URL.
> - Business Manager gives a Site Merchandiser a way to override the canonical target on a specific indexable filter URL - exact BM mechanism TBC, see Assumptions.
> - Canonical URL strips tracking/query parameters that aren't part of the page's own identity (e.g. UTM params) - exact allow/deny list TBC, see Assumptions.
> - Canonical tag always reflects the current storefront's own domain/locale prefix - never points cross-storefront.
> - Verified via view-source across at least one page of each template type (home, PDP, category, a paginated category page, and a filtered category page) on each storefront.

### SFCC-577 — "SEO — PLP SEO Copy Content Field (CMS-Editable, BM-Configurable)"
Status `To Do` · Labels `Custom`, `DMU-036`, `Squad-B`

Description, quoted:
> "As a Site Merchandiser, I want a CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level via Business Manager, so that SEO copy can be updated without a code deployment.
>
> This story covers the CMS content field integration and BM configurability. The Read More expand interaction and conditional background colour are covered by SFCC-95. The Shop By keyword tag links within the expanded accordion are covered by SFCC-579. Depends on SFCC-95."

**Acceptance criteria: `null`. AC count: 0.**

> **Also material to the audit.** SFCC-577 has no acceptance criteria at all. Its scope boundary is defined only by one description sentence. You cannot assert it covers per-filter metadata, because it does not currently assert it covers anything specific.

### SFCC-573 — "SEO — CollectionPage, BreadcrumbList & ItemList Schema (PLP)"
Status `To Do` · Labels `Custom`, `DMU-039`, `Squad-B`

Description, quoted:
> "As a Site Admin, I want CollectionPage, BreadcrumbList, and ItemList structured data schema implemented on all PLP pages, so that category pages are eligible for rich results and breadcrumb trails display in search.
>
> BreadcrumbList is the only one of the three with an actual Google Search rich-result feature - CollectionPage and ItemList are valid schema.org markup with no dedicated Google SERP enhancement today, but still useful for AI/GEO crawlers per DMU-043. The Sparro template dependency is narrowed to a couple of modelling preferences, not the base shape - see Technical Notes and Dependencies. Depends on breadcrumb component existing (SFCC-578) for the BreadcrumbList portion only - ItemList/CollectionPage don't share that blocker."

**Acceptance criteria — 4 discrete ACs**, quoted in full:
> - BreadcrumbList: itemListElement array of ListItem{position (1-indexed), name, item (URL) - item omitted on the final/current-page item per Google's spec}, sourced from whatever breadcrumb path SFCC-578's component computes.
> - ItemList: itemListElement array of ListItem{position, url, name} for each product currently rendered on the PLP page (paginated - only the current page's products, consistent with SFCC-562's per-page-canonical pagination rule) - buildable today from the existing productSearchResult data already available to product-list, independent of the breadcrumb component.
> - CollectionPage: name, description, url (canonical PLP URL per SFCC-562), wrapping the ItemList - confirm with Sparro whether they want this wrapper or a bare ItemList (both valid; Google has no dedicated CollectionPage rich result either way, so this is a modelling preference).
> - Filtered/faceted PLP variants that SFCC-562 canonicalizes to the base PLP do NOT get their own ItemList/CollectionPage describing the filtered subset - the schema always describes the canonical (unfiltered) product set, matching the declared canonical URL.

### AC count summary

| Story | AC count |
|---|---|
| SFCC-563 | **0** (null — merged into 562) |
| SFCC-562 | **9** |
| SFCC-577 | **0** (null) |
| SFCC-573 | **4** |

---

## How much of SFCC-724 is already covered? — my read

**SFCC-724's own description**, quoted:
> "As a Site Merchandiser, I want to flag specific filter combinations (e.g. Dresses + White) as indexable pages with their own clean URL and metadata, so that Zimmermann can rank for high-value search terms like "white dresses" without having to create and maintain a separate category for each one.
>
> Currently, all filtered PLP URLs canonicalise back to the base category page per DMU-023, meaning Google does not index them as standalone pages. This enhancement would allow a merchandiser to opt specific filter combinations into indexability via Business Manager, and set a unique title tag, meta description, and SEO paragraph per combination. The PWA Kit would then render the correct metadata for those URLs.
>
> Note: the SEO agency (Sparro / Tell No Lies) must define the URL structure rules and metadata templates before build can begin. This is a custom build — effort estimate required before prioritisation."

Labels: `DMU-023` only — **the same requirement ID as SFCC-562/563.**

### Verdict: roughly **one of five** component parts is genuinely covered. The half the ticket is named after is not.

| SFCC-724 component | Covered? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. BM opt-in to indexability per filter combo | **YES — real overlap** | SFCC-562 AC 6 |
| 2. Canonical behaviour for opted-in combos | **YES — real overlap** | SFCC-562 AC 5 |
| 3. Clean URL for the filter combination | **NO** | Undefined everywhere |
| 4. Per-filter title tag | **NO** | SFCC-568 is category-object-bound |
| 5. Per-filter meta description | **NO** | SFCC-569 is category-object-bound |
| 6. Per-filter SEO paragraph | **ADJACENT, not equivalent** | SFCC-577, storefront-level, 0 ACs |

**The two AC lines that genuinely overlap**, quoted from SFCC-562:

> "Facet combinations Tell No Lies/Sparro confirm as having real standalone search demand (see SFCC-571 dependency) are excluded from that rule and get a self-referencing canonical instead, per SFCC-571's per-facet-type split - never both a robots.txt block and a canonical on the same URL."

> "Business Manager gives a Site Merchandiser a way to override the canonical target on a specific indexable filter URL - exact BM mechanism TBC, see Assumptions."

Between them these cover *"allow a merchandiser to opt specific filter combinations into indexability via Business Manager"* — genuinely the same capability. If SFCC-724 is estimated as if that were greenfield, it is double-counted against SFCC-562.

**What is NOT covered — and I checked this against the actual implementation source, not just the titles.** SFCC-724's *"set a unique title tag, meta description, and SEO paragraph per combination"* has no home:

- **SFCC-568** (Title Tag Generation) AC 1, quoted: *"PDP and PLP/category page title tags render from product.pageTitle / category.pageTitle (already implemented) - confirm this already satisfies the requirement for those two templates with no further PWA code work."*
- **SFCC-569** (Meta Description) AC 1, quoted: *"PDP and PLP/category meta description already render from product.pageDescription / category.pageDescription (and pageMetaTags where set) - confirm this already satisfies the requirement for those two templates."*

Both source metadata from the **SFCC category object**. A facet combination is not a category — that is the entire premise of SFCC-724 (*"without having to create and maintain a separate category for each one"*). So there is structurally nowhere for per-filter metadata to live under the current design. **This is net-new build, and it is the larger half of the ticket.**

- **SFCC-577** covers the SEO copy field at *"all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level"* — per-storefront-per-category, not per-filter-combination. With zero ACs, its boundary is undefined; it cannot be relied on as covering the per-filter case without someone writing that AC.

### Three risks I'd raise before this estimate is signed off

1. **`SFCC-571`'s "per-facet-type split" does not exist.** SFCC-562 AC 5 defers to it explicitly. SFCC-571's actual ACs say only: *"Filtered/faceted PLP query parameters are disallowed via a parameter-pattern rule - exact pattern TBC, see Assumptions."* **Dangling cross-reference.** The indexable-facet allow-list that both SFCC-562 and SFCC-724 depend on is not written down in either story, or anywhere in Confluence. Both are blocked on the same undelivered Tell No Lies/Sparro input.

2. **SFCC-724 and SFCC-562 both carry label `DMU-023`, and they specify opposite behaviours** — 562 suppresses filtered PLPs, 724 promotes selected ones. They are the rule and its exception filed as independent tickets against one requirement ID. Per your own duplicate-detection heuristic (shared DMU-/SPR- labels), this is exactly the shape that needs reconciling before either is estimated.

3. **SFCC-573 AC 4 will conflict with SFCC-724 if 724 ships.** Quoted: *"Filtered/faceted PLP variants that SFCC-562 canonicalizes to the base PLP do NOT get their own ItemList/CollectionPage describing the filtered subset."* An indexable, self-canonical filter page under SFCC-724 falls outside that carve-out and **would need its own ItemList/CollectionPage** describing the filtered subset — unscoped work in SFCC-573, not counted in either estimate.
